Period under review: June 2025. Ledger A is the purchase ledger kept by Galtolm Trading for the supplier Yorvevi Foods, and ledger B is the supplier statement that Yorvevi Foods issued to Galtolm Trading.

Matching conventions:
(1) Each entry of A is matched only with the lines of B that carry exactly the same doc number.
(2) The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
(3) A line of B that carries no doc number and no payment run number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
(4) B is kept by the other side, so every amount figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
(5) An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of amount figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for method WIRE and for entries with a payment run number.
(6) Dates may differ by at most 2 days in either direction; a gap of exactly 2 days is still accepted, a larger one is not.
(7) Two B lines with the same doc number stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its amount multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
(8) Entries of A with method WIRE reach B less a transfer charge of 2.50 each: the amount figure on the B line is 2.50 smaller in size than the amount figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other method has a deduction.
(9) B combines the A entries of one payment run number into one line with that number as doc number and their summed amount, sign reversed; their own doc number values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
(10) When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the amount of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

q.instructions: Which waiting case do the rules put at the position asked for in the state?

state:
Location: Mabavenn town hall, service desk 8
Time now: 09:30

The order is fixed by these rules, taken in the order given:
1. A visitor that has waited at least 50 minutes moves up one class.
2. The visitors are taken class by class, smallest class number first.
3. Within the same class, visitors whose booked time is due go first.
4. Last tie-break: the visitor with the lower ticket number goes first.

Conventions:
- Read the rules from top to bottom; a later rule is used only to separate visitors that every earlier rule leaves level.
- First apply rule 1 to each visitor; from rule 2 on, the word "class" stands for the changed class.
- A visitor that moves up one class gets the next smaller class number, for instance 3 instead of 4.
- No visitor can go higher than class 1; a visitor of class 1 stays in class 1 whatever applies to it.
- After a class change a visitor is treated like every other visitor of its new class.
- To get the waiting time, subtract the "entered" time from the current time (in minutes; same day; 24-hour clock).
- "At least 50 minutes" includes exactly 50 minutes; 49 minutes are not enough.
- A booked time counts as due from its own minute on, that is, when it is not later than the current time.
- The rule only separates due from not due: how early the booked time was does not matter, and "-" or a later time counts as not due.
- The order is worked out once, for all waiting visitors, at the current time; first, second and third are positions in this one order.
- Whatever the list shows that no rule uses (a column, a flag) is for information only.
- The ticket number is the number after the dash; no two visitors have the same one.

q.instructions: Does the proposed set install cleanly in the target environment?

state:
Proposed install on gostpho-11, a robot controller: the components pinned at the end, taken from the component depot below.

How to read the entries and when a set is clean:
- Versions are ordered part by part as integers, not as text: 3.10.0 is later than 3.9.9, and 2.0.0 is later than 1.15.2. Runtime versions (two parts) follow the same order, so 4.11 is later than 4.9.
- After a component name come one or more bounds separated by commas, and every bound must hold: >=V at least V, >V newer than V, <=V at most V, <V older than V, ==V exactly V, !=V any version except V.
- A clean install needs all of the following: each pin is a version that the component depot lists; for each pinned version, each component it needs is pinned too, at a version inside the stated bounds; the runtime of the environment satisfies the runtime bounds of all pinned versions.
- Only the entries of the pinned versions count; what the component depot says about other versions plays no part.
- No component is added automatically: if a pinned version requires a component that has no pin, that requirement fails.
- Pinning a component that nothing needs is allowed, but the entry of that pinned version must still be met.
- Runtime bounds are checked against the runtime of the target environment; a version marked 'any' runs on every runtime.

state:
Period under review: August 2026. Ledger A is the timesheet of the Selvolm team, and ledger B is the client hours log signed off by Hoskand Ceramics.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
Rule 1: Each entry of A is matched only with the lines of B that carry exactly the same sheet id.
Rule 2: B is kept by the other side, so every hours figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
Rule 3: An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of hours figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for mode TRAVEL and for entries with a roll-up number.
Rule 4: Dates may differ by at most 2 days in either direction; a gap of exactly 2 days is still accepted, a larger one is not.
Rule 5: Two B lines with the same sheet id stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its hours multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
Rule 6: A line for an entry with mode TRAVEL is 0.50 h smaller in size in B (travel deduction; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 0.50 h in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 0.50 h. Other mode values carry no deduction.
Rule 7: B combines the A entries of one roll-up number into one line with that number as sheet id and their summed hours, sign reversed; their own sheet id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
Rule 8: A combined line that is short by the exact hours of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the roll-up is fine.
Rule 9: Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
Rule 10: A line of B that carries no sheet id and no roll-up number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

Ordering rules (apply them in this order):
1. Waiting at least 90 minutes lifts a request by one class.
2. The flag "blocked" moves a request up one class.
3. Lower class number first.
4. Within the same class, requests whose callback slot is due go first.
5. Of two requests, the one with fewer minutes under "effort" is ahead.
6. Lower ticket number first.

Conventions:
- An earlier rule always outranks a later one; a later rule only breaks ties that remain after the rules above it.
- Rules 1 and 2 do not order anything by themselves: they set the class that the later rules use.
- Moving up one class means that the class number becomes one smaller (class 3 becomes class 2).
- Class 1 is the top: a request never moves above class 1.
- After a class change a request is treated like every other request of its new class.
- The waiting time of a request is counted in minutes from the time under "logged" to the current time; all times are today, on a 24-hour clock.
- The limit itself counts: 90 minutes of waiting are enough, one minute less is not.
- The two class changes are not cumulative: meeting rule 1 and rule 2 counts the same as meeting one of them.
- Due means that the time under "callback" has been reached: it is equal to the current time or before it.
- The rule only separates due from not due: how early the callback slot was does not matter, and "-" or a later time counts as not due.
- The order is worked out once, for all waiting requests, at the current time; first, second and third are positions in this one order.
- Whatever the list shows that no rule uses (a column, a flag) is for information only.

A pipeline runner called nuvwim-44 is to receive plugins from the plugin registry.

How to read the entries and when a set is clean:
1. To order two versions, compare the first numbers, then the second, then the third, always as whole numbers, so 0.10.1 comes after 0.9.8 and 1.2.10 after 1.2.9. Runtime versions (two parts) follow the same order, so 4.11 is later than 4.9.
2. After a plugin name come one or more bounds separated by commas, and every bound must hold: >=V at least V, >V newer than V, <=V at most V, <V older than V, ==V exactly V, !=V any version except V.
3. The proposed set installs cleanly when every pinned version is listed in the plugin registry, every requirement of every pinned version names a plugin that is pinned at a version meeting all of its bounds, the runtime of the target environment meets every runtime bound of every pinned version, and no conflict entry of a pinned version applies to another pin.
4. Only the entries of the pinned versions count; what the plugin registry says about other versions plays no part.
5. Only pinned plugins get installed; a required plugin that has no pin counts as unmet.
6. A pin that no pinned version requires does no harm by itself; its own entry is checked like that of every other pin.
7. Runtime bounds are checked against the runtime of the target environment; a version marked 'any' runs on every runtime.
8. Conflicts ('cannot be combined with'): a pinned version that names a plugin P with a bound blocks the set exactly when P is pinned at a version meeting that bound; if P has no pin, or its pin misses the bound, nothing happens.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

state:
Reconciliation for September 2025. Ledger A is the purchase ledger of Prelevi Textiles for the supplier Ulstont Foods; ledger B is the supplier statement that Ulstont Foods issued to Prelevi Textiles.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
1. An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their doc number values are identical, character for character.
2. Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
3. A line of B that carries no doc number and no payment run number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
4. B is kept by the other side, so every amount figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
5. An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of amount figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for method WIRE and for entries with a payment run number.
6. A B line dated more than 3 days before or after its A entry is not a valid match, so that entry does not reconcile; 3 days or less is fine.
7. Two B lines with the same doc number stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its amount multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
8. Entries of A with method WIRE reach B less a transfer charge of 1.20 each: the amount figure on the B line is 1.20 smaller in size than the amount figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other method has a deduction.
9. Entries of A that share a payment run number appear in B as one line whose doc number is that number and whose amount figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
10. If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the amount of one entry of the payment run, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the payment run reconcile.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

The order is fixed by these rules, taken in the order given:
1. Waiting at least 50 minutes lifts a request by one class.
2. Any request carrying the flag "outage" is lifted by one class.
3. The requests are taken class by class, smallest class number first.
4. The request with the shorter estimated effort goes first.
5. If requests are still level, the lower ticket number is ahead.

Conventions:
- An earlier rule always outranks a later one; a later rule only breaks ties that remain after the rules above it.
- First apply rules 1 and 2 to each request; from rule 3 on, the word "class" stands for the changed class.
- "Up one class" is the class number minus 1; for example, class 4 turns into class 3.
- Class 1 is the top: a request never moves above class 1.
- After a class change a request is treated like every other request of its new class.
- The waiting time of a request is counted in minutes from the time under "logged" to the current time; all times are today, on a 24-hour clock.
- A wait of exactly 50 minutes counts as at least 50 minutes.
- The two class changes are cumulative: meeting rule 1 and rule 2 means two classes up, with class 1 as the limit.
- Rank every waiting request once, as things stand at the current time; the position asked for is a place in that ranking.

Matching conventions:
(1) Pairing goes by note id alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same note id.
(2) B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
(3) B may hold extra lines whose note id matches nothing in A (no entry, no load number); they play no part.

state:
The two records below cover March 2025: ledger A, the stock system of the Yorvevi store, and ledger B, the receiving log kept at the Yorvure depot.

Matching conventions:
1. Each entry of A is matched only with the lines of B that carry exactly the same movement id.
2. B is kept by the other side, so every quantity figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
3. A pair agrees when the B quantity figure equals the A quantity figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, route SAMPLE entries and pallet entries.
4. The date of a B line may be up to 3 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 3 days means the entry does not reconcile.
5. B sometimes splits one entry into two lines with the same movement id; together they must give the entry's quantity with the opposite sign, and each line must be inside the date tolerance.
6. Entries of A with route SAMPLE reach B less a retained test sample of 2 units each: the quantity figure on the B line is 2 units smaller in size than the quantity figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other route has a deduction.
7. Several A entries with the same pallet number are shown in B as a single line carrying that number in the movement id column, for the total of those entries with the opposite sign (date rule as usual, against their common date).
8. If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the quantity of one entry of the pallet, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the pallet reconcile.
9. The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
10. B may hold extra lines whose movement id matches nothing in A (no entry, no pallet number); they play no part.

At most one entry of A fails to reconcile.

How to read the entries and when a set is clean:
- Versions are compared number by number from the left, each number as a whole number: 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.3, and 2.0.0 is newer than 1.12.7. The same holds for the two-part runtime versions: 2.10 comes after 2.9.
- Each bound is an operator and a version: >= (that version or newer), > (newer only), <= (that version or older), < (older only), == (only that version), != (every version but that one); a list of bounds is met only when each bound is met.
- The set is clean only if the extension catalogue lists every pinned version, every requirement of a pinned version is met by the pin of the required extension, each runtime bound of a pinned version holds for the environment's runtime, and none of the pinned versions has a conflict entry that applies to another pin.
- Requirements and other entries of versions without a pin do not matter.
- No extension is added automatically: if a pinned version requires an extension that has no pin, that requirement fails.
- A pin that no pinned version requires does no harm by itself; its own entry is checked like that of every other pin.
- A runtime bound of a pinned version is met when the runtime of the target environment satisfies it; 'any' sets no runtime bound.
- An entry 'clashes with P B' under a pinned version means that the set fails when P is pinned at a version meeting the bound B; it does not matter which of the two lists it, and an entry about an extension without a pin, or whose pin misses B, does no harm.

state:
Reconciliation for July 2025. Ledger A is the cash book kept by Coskont Ceramics; ledger B is the bank statement that Dulvansa Cooperative Bank sent to Coskont Ceramics.

How the two ledgers are matched:
Rule 1: Pairing goes by reference alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same reference.
Rule 2: B is kept by the other side, so every amount figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
Rule 3: An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of amount figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for channel CARD and for entries with a lodgement number.
Rule 4: Dates may differ by at most 5 days in either direction; a gap of exactly 5 days is still accepted, a larger one is not.
Rule 5: An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its reference; it then reconciles when the two amount figures add up to its amount with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
Rule 6: A line for an entry with channel CARD is 0.45 smaller in size in B (processing fee; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 0.45 in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 0.45. Other channel values carry no deduction.
Rule 7: Several A entries with the same lodgement number are shown in B as a single line carrying that number in the reference column, for the total of those entries with the opposite sign (date rule as usual, against their common date).
Rule 8: When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the amount of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.
Rule 9: The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
Rule 10: Lines of B whose reference is neither a reference of A nor a lodgement number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

state:
The two records below cover March 2025: ledger A, the stock system of the Yorvevi store, and ledger B, the receiving log kept at the Yorvure depot.

Matching conventions:
1. Each entry of A is matched only with the lines of B that carry exactly the same movement id.
2. B is kept by the other side, so every quantity figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
3. A pair agrees when the B quantity figure equals the A quantity figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, route SAMPLE entries and pallet entries.
4. The date of a B line may be up to 3 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 3 days means the entry does not reconcile.
5. B sometimes splits one entry into two lines with the same movement id; together they must give the entry's quantity with the opposite sign, and each line must be inside the date tolerance.
6. Entries of A with route SAMPLE reach B less a retained test sample of 2 units each: the quantity figure on the B line is 2 units smaller in size than the quantity figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other route has a deduction.
7. Several A entries with the same pallet number are shown in B as a single line carrying that number in the movement id column, for the total of those entries with the opposite sign (date rule as usual, against their common date).
8. If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the quantity of one entry of the pallet, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the pallet reconcile.
9. The order of the lines in B carries no meaning and differs from the order of A.
10. B may hold extra lines whose movement id matches nothing in A (no entry, no pallet number); they play no part.

At most one entry of A fails to reconcile.

Permission data of a fictional code hosting service, followed by the rules that govern it.

How access is decided:
1. An assignment gives one role to one user or to one group. An assignment to a group counts for every user on that group's member list and for nobody else.
2. Assignments reach downward only: the namespace where an assignment is made and everything below it, however deep, are covered; namespaces beside it or above it are not.
3. Holding a role permits the actions on that role's list.
4. Where the inclusion list states that one action includes another, permission for the first counts as permission for the second, and likewise onward along several such lines. There are no unlisted inclusions, and the included action never brings the including one.
5. A request is allowed only when an assignment whose role the requester holds covers the requested namespace and that role allows the requested action.

Refund policy

General provisions
- If two applicable rules lead to different outcomes, the lower-numbered rule decides.
- By default a request is denied unless a rule says otherwise.

Rules
1. If the refund amount is 1500 EUR or more, the request is escalated to a human reviewer.
2. If the case has the bank dispute flag set to no and the fraud alert flag is no, the request is approved.
3. If the fraud alert flag is set to yes and the record shows yes for the bank dispute flag, the request is denied.
4. If the record shows yes for the fraud alert flag and the refund amount is between 300 and 1500 EUR inclusive, the request is escalated to a human reviewer.
5. If the refund amount is greater than 750 EUR and the plan tier is not any of T2 or T1, the request is denied.

9. If the case has the item returned flag set to no and the case has the fraud alert flag set to yes, the request is denied.
10. If the record shows no for the proof of purchase flag and the number of earlier refunds is within 2 to 4 with both limits included, the request is escalated to a human reviewer.
11. If the number of earlier refunds is below 2 and the plan tier is not one of T1, T3 or T2, the request is approved.
12. If the refund amount is under 100 EUR and the number of earlier refunds is 1 or less, the request is approved.

Exceptions
- Rule 4 is waived if the number of earlier refunds is less than 1.
- Rule 12 is waived if the case has the item returned flag set to no.

state:
Reconciliation for January 2025. Ledger A is the stock system in which the Hoskolm store books its movements; ledger B is the receiving log of the Coskast depot.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
1. An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their movement id values are identical, character for character.
2. Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
3. An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of quantity figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for route SAMPLE and for entries with a pallet number.
4. The date of a B line may be up to 3 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 3 days means the entry does not reconcile.
5. An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its movement id; it then reconciles when the two quantity figures add up to its quantity with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
6. Entries of A with route SAMPLE reach B less a retained test sample of 1 units each: the quantity figure on the B line is 1 units smaller in size than the quantity figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other route has a deduction.
7. B combines the A entries of one pallet number into one line with that number as movement id and their summed quantity, sign reversed; their own movement id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
8. A combined line that is short by the exact quantity of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the pallet is fine.
9. B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
10. Lines of B whose movement id is neither a movement id of A nor a pallet number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

- A booked time counts as due from its own minute on, that is, when it is not later than the current time.
- The rule only separates due from not due: how early the booked time was does not matter, and "-" or a later time counts as not due.
- The order is worked out once, for all waiting visitors, at the current time; first, second and third are positions in this one order.

- flag: a marker noted for the job; "-" means no marker
- pickup: time of the agreed pickup ("-" = none)
- bench: expected bench time in minutes

Ordering rules (apply them in this order):
1. Once the waiting time of a job is at least 25 minutes, it is moved up one class.
2. Any job carrying the flag "safety" is lifted by one class.
3. Lower class number first.
4. Inside a class, every job whose pickup time is due precedes every job whose pickup time is not due.
5. The job with the shorter bench time goes first.
6. Last tie-break: the job with the lower ticket number goes first.

Notes on the rules:
- Read the rules from top to bottom; a later rule is used only to separate jobs that every earlier rule leaves level.
- Rules 1 and 2 change the class of a job and are applied to every job before anything is compared; in the rules after them, "class" means the class after these changes.
- "Up one class" is the class number minus 1; for example, class 4 turns into class 3.
- There is no class above class 1, so a change that would lead above class 1 stops at class 1.
- After a class change a job is treated like every other job of its new class.
- Waiting time = current time minus the time under "checkin", in minutes (same day, 24-hour clock).
- "At least 25 minutes" includes exactly 25 minutes; 24 minutes are not enough.
- Rules 1 and 2 add up: a job that meets both moves up two classes (but never above class 1).
- A pickup time counts as due from its own minute on, that is, when it is not later than the current time.
- Two jobs that are both due, or both not due (no pickup time, or one that is still to come), stay level under this rule.
- The order is worked out once, for all waiting jobs, at the current time; first, second and third are positions in this one order.
- Columns and flags that no rule mentions have no effect on the order.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

state:
Reconciliation for August 2026. Ledger A is the stock system of the Hoskure store; ledger B is the receiving log of the Tarnont depot.

Matching conventions:
(1) Each entry of A is matched only with the lines of B that carry exactly the same movement id.
(2) B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
(3) B may hold extra lines whose movement id matches nothing in A (no entry, no pallet number); they play no part.
(4) B is kept by the other side, so every quantity figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
(5) An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of quantity figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for route SAMPLE and for entries with a pallet number.
(6) A B line dated more than 1 day before or after its A entry is not a valid match, so that entry does not reconcile; 1 day or less is fine.
(7) An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its movement id; it then reconciles when the two quantity figures add up to its quantity with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
(8) For every A entry whose route is SAMPLE, B takes a fixed retained test sample of 4 units per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 4 units, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other route are not reduced.
(9) Entries of A that share a pallet number appear in B as one line whose movement id is that number and whose quantity figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
(10) If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the quantity of one entry of the pallet, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the pallet reconcile.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

- flag: at most one marker per vessel ("-" = none)
- window: start of the booked berth window; "-" means none
- turnaround: expected turnaround time in minutes, whole minutes

Rules, applied in the order given:
1. A vessel that has waited at least 45 minutes moves up one class.
2. Any vessel carrying the flag "tidal" is lifted by one class.
3. A vessel with a lower class number goes before a vessel with a higher class number.
4. Inside a class, every vessel whose berth window is due precedes every vessel whose berth window is not due.
5. Of two vessels, the one with the earlier time under "anchored" is ahead.
6. If vessels are still level, the lower ticket number is ahead.

Conventions:
- Read the rules from top to bottom; a later rule is used only to separate vessels that every earlier rule leaves level.
- Rules 1 and 2 change the class of a vessel and are applied to every vessel before anything is compared; in the rules after them, "class" means the class after these changes.
- "Up one class" is the class number minus 1; for example, class 4 turns into class 3.
- Class 1 is the top: a vessel never moves above class 1.
- A vessel that has moved up is an ordinary member of its new class; nothing else about it changes.
- To get the waiting time, subtract the "anchored" time from the current time (in minutes; same day; 24-hour clock).
- The limit itself counts: 45 minutes of waiting are enough, one minute less is not.
- Rules 1 and 2 do not add up: a vessel that meets both still moves up one class only.
- A berth window counts as due from its own minute on, that is, when it is not later than the current time.
- The rule only separates due from not due: how early the berth window was does not matter, and "-" or a later time counts as not due.
- All positions (first, second, third) refer to a single order computed at the current time; the clock is not moved in between.
- Columns and flags that no rule mentions have no effect on the order.
- The ticket number is the number after the dash; no two vessels have the same one.

state:
Proposed install on skelosk-19, a robot controller: the components pinned at the end, taken from the component depot below.

Rules of this check:
* To order two versions, compare the first numbers, then the second, then the third, always as whole numbers, so 0.10.1 comes after 0.9.8 and 1.2.10 after 1.2.9. Runtime versions have two numbers and are compared the same way (3.10 is newer than 3.9).
* Bounds read as follows: >= at least, > strictly newer, <= at most, < strictly older, == exactly this version, != anything but this version; where several bounds follow one name, all of them apply.
* The set is clean only if the component depot lists every pinned version, every requirement of a pinned version is met by the pin of the required component, each runtime bound of a pinned version holds for the environment's runtime, and none of the pinned versions has a conflict entry that applies to another pin.
* Entries of versions that are not pinned are irrelevant.
* No component is added automatically: if a pinned version requires a component that has no pin, that requirement fails.
* A pin that no pinned version requires does no harm by itself; its own entry is checked like that of every other pin.
* The environment's runtime must satisfy each runtime bound of each pinned version ('any' means no bound).
* An entry 'conflicts with P B' under a pinned version means that the set fails when P is pinned at a version meeting the bound B; it does not matter which of the two lists it, and an entry about a component without a pin, or whose pin misses B, does no harm.

What follows are the access rules and the current permission records of an invented document workspace.

Rules:
- A role is held by the user an assignment names or, when it names a group, by every member of that group. The members of a group are the users on its list plus all members of each group on its list, and so on through further nesting. A group that is nested inside another gains no members from the group that contains it.
- Assignments reach downward only: the folder where an assignment is made and everything below it, however deep, are covered; folders beside it or above it are not.
- Exception for sealed folders: an assignment never passes into a sealed folder from a folder above it, so the sealed folder and everything below it stay out of its reach. A seal does nothing to an assignment made at the sealed folder or below it, and nothing to folders that are not inside the sealed folder.
- A role allows the actions listed for it. A role that extends another role also allows everything the other role allows, including what that role gets from a role it extends. Extension works one way only: the extended role gains nothing.
- Actions can include other actions, exactly as listed. Being allowed an action means being allowed every action it includes, directly or through a chain of listed inclusions. An inclusion is never read backwards, and actions without a listed link do not include each other.
- A deny entry forbids one action to one user, or to all direct and nested members of one group, on one folder and all folders below it; seals make no difference to deny entries. When an entry matches the requester, the exact action and the folder, the request is refused whatever the assignments say. An entry for a different action never matches, and inclusions between actions are ignored for deny entries.

state.policy:
Rules for expense claims

(1) A request for which the number of claims this quarter is below 3 and the pre-approval flag is yes is approved.
(2) A request for which the pre-approval flag is yes and the case has the company card use flag set to yes is approved.
(3) A request for which the claim amount is at least 1000 EUR is denied.
(4) A request for which the claim amount does not exceed 25 EUR and the grade on record is G5 and the record shows yes for the company card use flag is approved.
(5) A request for which the record shows no for the pre-approval flag and the grade on record is G2 is escalated to a human reviewer.
(6) A request for which the claim amount is 1000 EUR or higher is escalated to a human reviewer.
(7) A request for which the grade is either G3 or G5 and the time since the expense is greater than 60 days is denied.
(8) A request for which the record shows yes for the duplicate suspicion flag is denied.
(9) A request for which the time since the expense is greater than 45 days and the pre-approval flag is set to no is denied.
(10) A request for which the time since the expense exceeds 30 days and the cost centre is not among CC-512, CC-204 or CC-117 is escalated to a human reviewer.
(11) A request for which the number of claims this quarter is 3 or more and the grade is among G3, G5 or G2 and the cost centre is CC-455 is escalated to a human reviewer.
(12) A request for which the number of claims this quarter is less than 2 and the cost centre equals CC-512 and the case has the company card use flag set to yes is approved.

Rule 4 is waived if the cost centre is any of CC-204 or CC-455 and the time since the expense is at least 30 days.
Rule 3 is waived if the number of claims this quarter is at most 5.
Rule 5 is waived if the time since the expense is 30 days or less.
Rule 9 is waived if the company card use flag is yes.

Conflicting rules are resolved in favour of the rule with the smaller number.
A request that no rule covers is denied.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

state:
The two records below cover January 2025: ledger A, the dispatch register of the Ulstora plant, and ledger B, the weighbridge record of the haulier Bralolm Transport.

How the two ledgers are matched:
1. An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their note id values are identical, character for character.
2. Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
3. A pair agrees when the B weight figure equals the A weight figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, packing PALLET entries and load entries.
4. A B line dated more than 5 days before or after its A entry is not a valid match, so that entry does not reconcile; 5 days or less is fine.
5. B sometimes splits one entry into two lines with the same note id; together they must give the entry's weight with the opposite sign, and each line must be inside the date tolerance.
6. For every A entry whose packing is PALLET, B takes a fixed pallet tare of 15.0 kg per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 15.0 kg, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other packing are not reduced.
7. B combines the A entries of one load number into one line with that number as note id and their summed weight, sign reversed; their own note id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
8. If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the weight of one entry of the load, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the load reconcile.
9. B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
10. B may hold extra lines whose note id matches nothing in A (no entry, no load number); they play no part.

Either exactly one entry of A does not reconcile, or every entry does.

state:
Service point: Kesivar minor-injuries unit, front counter 3
Time now: 16:16

Rules, applied in the order given:
1. Once the waiting time of a patient is at least 35 minutes, it is moved up one class.
2. A patient with the flag "frail" counts one class more urgent.
3. The patients are taken class by class, smallest class number first.
4. Among patients of one class, a patient with a due booked slot is ahead of a patient without a due one.
5. Earlier arrival first.
6. Last tie-break: the patient with the lower ticket number goes first.

Notes on the rules:
- An earlier rule always outranks a later one; a later rule only breaks ties that remain after the rules above it.
- Rules 1 and 2 do not order anything by themselves: they set the class that the later rules use.
- "Up one class" is the class number minus 1; for example, class 4 turns into class 3.
- There is no class above class 1, so a change that would lead above class 1 stops at class 1.
- After a class change a patient is treated like every other patient of its new class.
- To get the waiting time, subtract the "arrived" time from the current time (in minutes; same day; 24-hour clock).
- "At least 35 minutes" includes exactly 35 minutes; 34 minutes are not enough.
- Both class changes can apply to the same patient; it then moves up two classes in total, stopping at class 1.
- Due means that the time under "slot" has been reached: it is equal to the current time or before it.
- The patients with a due booked slot are level with each other under this rule (the times under "slot" are not compared), and so are the patients without a due one.
- Rank every waiting patient once, as things stand at the current time; the position asked for is a place in that ranking.
- Columns and flags that no rule mentions have no effect on the order.
- Every patient has its own ticket number: the number that follows the dash in the identifier.

state:
Location: Rudivar port control, berth desk 9
Clock at the moment of the decision: 15:10

Ordering rules (apply them in this order):
1. Waiting at least 75 minutes lifts a vessel by one class.
2. A vessel with the flag "reefer" counts one class more urgent.
3. Lower class number first.
4. Within the same class, vessels whose berth window is due go first.
5. If vessels are still level, the lower ticket number is ahead.

Conventions:
- The rules are applied in the order given: a rule decides only between vessels that all rules before it leave level.
- First apply rules 1 and 2 to each vessel; from rule 3 on, the word "class" stands for the changed class.
- Moving up one class means that the class number becomes one smaller (class 3 becomes class 2).
- No vessel can go higher than class 1; a vessel of class 1 stays in class 1 whatever applies to it.
- A vessel that has moved up is an ordinary member of its new class; nothing else about it changes.
- The waiting time of a vessel is counted in minutes from the time under "anchored" to the current time; all times are today, on a 24-hour clock.
- "At least 75 minutes" includes exactly 75 minutes; 74 minutes are not enough.
- Both class changes can apply to the same vessel; it then moves up two classes in total, stopping at class 1.
- Due means that the time under "window" has been reached: it is equal to the current time or before it.
- The rule only separates due from not due: how early the berth window was does not matter, and "-" or a later time counts as not due.
- Rank every waiting vessel once, as things stand at the current time; the position asked for is a place in that ranking.
- Whatever the list shows that no rule uses (a column, a flag) is for information only.

state:
Reconciliation for September 2025. Ledger A is the purchase ledger of Prelevi Textiles for the supplier Ulstont Foods; ledger B is the supplier statement that Ulstont Foods issued to Prelevi Textiles.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
1. An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their doc number values are identical, character for character.
2. Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
3. A line of B that carries no doc number and no payment run number of A is left aside; it affects no entry.
4. B is kept by the other side, so every amount figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
5. An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of amount figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for method WIRE and for entries with a payment run number.
6. A B line dated more than 3 days before or after its A entry is not a valid match, so that entry does not reconcile; 3 days or less is fine.
7. Two B lines with the same doc number stand for one entry of A; the entry reconciles when their sum equals its amount multiplied by -1 and neither line breaks the date rule.
8. Entries of A with method WIRE reach B less a transfer charge of 1.20 each: the amount figure on the B line is 1.20 smaller in size than the amount figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other method has a deduction.
9. Entries of A that share a payment run number appear in B as one line whose doc number is that number and whose amount figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
10. If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the amount of one entry of the payment run, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the payment run reconcile.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

Rules:
- A role is held by the user an assignment names or, when it names a group, by every member of that group. The members of a group are the users on its list plus all members of each group on its list, and so on through further nesting. A group that is nested inside another gains no members from the group that contains it.
- The role of an assignment is valid on the folder named in the assignment and on all folders below that folder at any depth, not on any other folder.
- Sealing cuts off what comes from above. If the requested folder is a sealed folder or lies below one, an assignment made above that sealed folder does not cover it. Assignments made at the sealed folder or below it work as usual, and a sealed folder elsewhere in the tree has no effect.
- Holding a role permits the actions on its own list and, when the role extends a second role, every action the second role permits (its own list and whatever it takes over by extension). The second role takes over nothing from the first.
- Where the inclusion list states that one action includes another, permission for the first counts as permission for the second, and likewise onward along several such lines. There are no unlisted inclusions, and the included action never brings the including one.
- A deny entry forbids one action to one user, or to all direct and nested members of one group, on one folder and all folders below it; seals make no difference to deny entries. When an entry matches the requester, the exact action and the folder, the request is refused whatever the assignments say. An entry for a different action never matches, and inclusions between actions are ignored for deny entries.

What is booked on another day has no effect on the request. The request lasts from its start time for the stated number of minutes. Capacity: the number of students plus one for the tutor (who is not listed among the students) must not exceed the seats of the room; equal is allowed. The tutor and all students are busy for the whole booking, and nobody may be in two bookings that overlap on the same day, whatever the rooms. Bookings that only touch are fine for a person: the reset gap is for rooms, not for people. Opening hours are binding: start not earlier than the opening time of the room, end not later than its closing time, equality allowed.

state:
A field controller called sorkenk-44 is to receive modules from the module feed.

Conventions:
1. Versions are compared number by number from the left, each number as a whole number: 1.10.0 is newer than 1.9.3, and 2.0.0 is newer than 1.12.7. Runtime versions have two numbers and are compared the same way (3.10 is newer than 3.9).
2. Bounds read as follows: >= at least, > strictly newer, <= at most, < strictly older, == exactly this version, != anything but this version; where several bounds follow one name, all of them apply.
3. A clean install needs all of the following: each pin is a version that the module feed lists; for each pinned version, each module it needs is pinned too, at a version inside the stated bounds; the runtime of the environment satisfies the runtime bounds of all pinned versions; no pinned version has a 'clashes with' entry that applies to another pin.
4. Only the entries of the pinned versions count; what the module feed says about other versions plays no part.
5. Nothing is installed besides the pins, so a requirement on a module without a pin is not met.
6. Extra pins are fine: a pinned module that nothing requires is harmless as long as its own entry is satisfied.
7. Runtime bounds are checked against the runtime of the target environment; a version marked 'any' runs on every runtime.
8. If a pinned version has a 'clashes with' entry naming another module and that module is pinned at a version inside the given bound, the set is not clean (whichever side lists it); entries about modules that are not pinned, or whose pin lies outside the bound, are harmless.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

state:
Reconciliation for August 2026. Ledger A is the stock system of the Hoskure store; ledger B is the receiving log of the Tarnont depot.

Matching conventions:
(1) Each entry of A is matched only with the lines of B that carry exactly the same movement id.
(2) B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
(3) B may hold extra lines whose movement id matches nothing in A (no entry, no pallet number); they play no part.
(4) B is kept by the other side, so every quantity figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
(5) An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of quantity figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for route SAMPLE and for entries with a pallet number.
(6) A B line dated more than 1 day before or after its A entry is not a valid match, so that entry does not reconcile; 1 day or less is fine.
(7) An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its movement id; it then reconciles when the two quantity figures add up to its quantity with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
(8) For every A entry whose route is SAMPLE, B takes a fixed retained test sample of 4 units per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 4 units, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other route are not reduced.
(9) Entries of A that share a pallet number appear in B as one line whose movement id is that number and whose quantity figure is their total with the sign reversed; the date rule compares that line with the date the entries share.
(10) If such a combined line falls short of that total, in size, by exactly the quantity of one entry of the pallet, that entry was left out and does not reconcile; the other entries of the pallet reconcile.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

Rules, applied in the order given:
1. Waiting at least 30 minutes lifts a job by one class.
2. Lower class number first.
3. Among jobs of one class, a job with a due pickup time is ahead of a job without a due one.
4. Lower ticket number first.

Conventions:
- The rules are applied in the order given: a rule decides only between jobs that all rules before it leave level.
- Rule 1 changes the class of a job and is applied to every job before anything is compared; in the rules after it, "class" means the class after this change.
- Moving up one class means that the class number becomes one smaller (class 3 becomes class 2).

- Once moved, a job competes inside its new class on equal terms with the jobs already there.
- To get the waiting time, subtract the "checkin" time from the current time (in minutes; same day; 24-hour clock).
- "At least 30 minutes" includes exactly 30 minutes; 29 minutes are not enough.
- A pickup time counts as due from its own minute on, that is, when it is not later than the current time.
- The jobs with a due pickup time are level with each other under this rule (the times under "pickup" are not compared), and so are the jobs without a due one.
- Rank every waiting job once, as things stand at the current time; the position asked for is a place in that ranking.
- Columns and flags that no rule mentions have no effect on the order.

(1) Pairing goes by reference alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same reference.

state:
The two records below cover September 2025: ledger A, the dispatch register kept at the Nolvolm plant, and ledger B, the weighbridge record kept by the haulier Orstast Haulage.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
(1) Pairing goes by note id alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same note id.
(2) B is kept by the other side, so every weight figure appears there with the opposite sign: a plus in A is a minus in B and the other way round.
(3) An entry reconciles when the weight figure on its B line is its own weight figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with packing PALLET and entries with a load number follow their own rules below.
(4) The date of a B line may be up to 2 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 2 days means the entry does not reconcile.
(5) An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its note id; it then reconciles when the two weight figures add up to its weight with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
(6) Entries of A with packing PALLET reach B less a pallet tare of 25.0 kg each: the weight figure on the B line is 25.0 kg smaller in size than the weight figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other packing has a deduction.
(7) B combines the A entries of one load number into one line with that number as note id and their summed weight, sign reversed; their own note id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
(8) A combined line that is short by the exact weight of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the load is fine.
(9) B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
(10) Lines of B whose note id is neither a note id of A nor a load number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

At most one entry of A fails to reconcile.

The order is fixed by these rules, taken in the order given:
1. A visitor that has waited at least 45 minutes moves up one class.
2. A visitor with the flag "carer" counts one class more urgent.
3. A visitor with a lower class number goes before a visitor with a higher class number.
4. Of two visitors, the one with fewer minutes under "desk" is ahead.
5. Lower ticket number first.

How to read the rules:
- An earlier rule always outranks a later one; a later rule only breaks ties that remain after the rules above it.
- Rules 1 and 2 change the class of a visitor and are applied to every visitor before anything is compared; in the rules after them, "class" means the class after these changes.
- Moving up one class means that the class number becomes one smaller (class 3 becomes class 2).
- No visitor can go higher than class 1; a visitor of class 1 stays in class 1 whatever applies to it.
- A visitor that has moved up is an ordinary member of its new class; nothing else about it changes.
- The waiting time of a visitor is counted in minutes from the time under "entered" to the current time; all times are today, on a 24-hour clock.
- The limit itself counts: 45 minutes of waiting are enough, one minute less is not.
- A visitor moves up at most one class in total, even when both rule 1 and rule 2 apply to it.
- All positions (first, second, third) refer to a single order computed at the current time; the clock is not moved in between.
- Whatever the list shows that no rule uses (a column, a flag) is for information only.
- Every visitor has its own ticket number: the number that follows the dash in the identifier.

Ordering rules (apply them in this order):
1. Once the waiting time of a task is at least 35 minutes, it is moved up one class.
2. The flag "review" moves a task up one class.
3. The tasks are taken class by class, smallest class number first.
4. Among tasks of one class, a task with a due reserved start is ahead of a task without a due one.
5. The task with the shorter run time goes first.
6. Lower ticket number first.

Conventions:
- An earlier rule always outranks a later one; a later rule only breaks ties that remain after the rules above it.
- Rules 1 and 2 change the class of a task and are applied to every task before anything is compared; in the rules after them, "class" means the class after these changes.
- "Up one class" is the class number minus 1; for example, class 4 turns into class 3.
- Class 1 is the top: a task never moves above class 1.
- After a class change a task is treated like every other task of its new class.
- To get the waiting time, subtract the "submitted" time from the current time (in minutes; same day; 24-hour clock).
- The limit itself counts: 35 minutes of waiting are enough, one minute less is not.
- The two class changes are not cumulative: meeting rule 1 and rule 2 counts the same as meeting one of them.
- Due means that the time under "reserved" has been reached: it is equal to the current time or before it.
- Two tasks that are both due, or both not due (no reserved start, or one that is still to come), stay level under this rule.
- The order is worked out once, for all waiting tasks, at the current time; first, second and third are positions in this one order.

How to read the entries and when a set is clean:
1. Versions are ordered part by part as integers, not as text: 3.10.0 is later than 3.9.9, and 2.0.0 is later than 1.15.2. The same holds for the two-part runtime versions: 2.10 comes after 2.9.
2. Bounds read as follows: >= at least, > strictly newer, <= at most, < strictly older, == exactly this version, != anything but this version; where several bounds follow one name, all of them apply.
3. The set is clean only if the component depot lists every pinned version, every requirement of a pinned version is met by the pin of the required component, each runtime bound of a pinned version holds for the environment's runtime, and none of the pinned versions has a conflict entry that applies to another pin.
4. Requirements and other entries of versions without a pin do not matter.
5. Nothing is installed besides the pins, so a requirement on a component without a pin is not met.
6. A pin that no pinned version requires does no harm by itself; its own entry is checked like that of every other pin.
7. Runtime bounds are checked against the runtime of the target environment; a version marked 'any' runs on every runtime.
8. Conflicts ('conflicts with'): a pinned version that names a component P with a bound blocks the set exactly when P is pinned at a version meeting that bound; if P has no pin, or its pin misses the bound, nothing happens.

Ordering rules (apply them in this order):
1. Once the waiting time of a task is at least 35 minutes, it is moved up one class.
2. The flag "review" moves a task up one class.
3. The tasks are taken class by class, smallest class number first.
4. Among tasks of one class, a task with a due reserved start is ahead of a task without a due one.
5. The task with the shorter run time goes first.
6. Lower ticket number first.

Conventions:
- An earlier rule always outranks a later one; a later rule only breaks ties that remain after the rules above it.
- Rules 1 and 2 change the class of a task and are applied to every task before anything is compared; in the rules after them, "class" means the class after these changes.
- "Up one class" is the class number minus 1; for example, class 4 turns into class 3.
- Class 1 is the top: a task never moves above class 1.
- After a class change a task is treated like every other task of its new class.
- To get the waiting time, subtract the "submitted" time from the current time (in minutes; same day; 24-hour clock).
- The limit itself counts: 35 minutes of waiting are enough, one minute less is not.
- The two class changes are not cumulative: meeting rule 1 and rule 2 counts the same as meeting one of them.
- Due means that the time under "reserved" has been reached: it is equal to the current time or before it.
- Two tasks that are both due, or both not due (no reserved start, or one that is still to come), stay level under this rule.
- The order is worked out once, for all waiting tasks, at the current time; first, second and third are positions in this one order.
- Only what the rules name counts; any other column or flag changes nothing.

How access is decided:
- A role is held by the user an assignment names or, when it names a group, by every member of that group. The members of a group are the users on its list plus all members of each group on its list, and so on through further nesting. A group that is nested inside another gains no members from the group that contains it.
- An assignment is made at one folder. It covers that folder and every folder below it (directly or further down), and nothing else.
- Sealing cuts off what comes from above. If the requested folder is a sealed folder or lies below one, an assignment made above that sealed folder does not cover it. Assignments made at the sealed folder or below it work as usual, and a sealed folder elsewhere in the tree has no effect.
- The actions a role allows are its own actions plus the actions of the role it extends, plus those of the role that one extends, and so on. Nothing is passed in the opposite direction, from the extending role to the extended one.
- Actions can include other actions, exactly as listed. Being allowed an action means being allowed every action it includes, directly or through a chain of listed inclusions. An inclusion is never read backwards, and actions without a listed link do not include each other.
- A request is allowed only when an assignment whose role the requester holds covers the requested folder and that role allows the requested action.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

state:
Reconciliation for January 2025. Ledger A is the stock system in which the Hoskolm store books its movements; ledger B is the receiving log of the Coskast depot.

Conventions for this reconciliation:
1. An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their movement id values are identical, character for character.
2. Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
3. An entry of A is in order when its B line shows the same size of quantity figure with the opposite sign, inside the date tolerance. Exceptions follow below for split entries, for route SAMPLE and for entries with a pallet number.
4. The date of a B line may be up to 3 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 3 days means the entry does not reconcile.
5. An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its movement id; it then reconciles when the two quantity figures add up to its quantity with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
6. Entries of A with route SAMPLE reach B less a retained test sample of 1 units each: the quantity figure on the B line is 1 units smaller in size than the quantity figure in A (the size of a figure is its value without the sign), and its sign is reversed. This holds for plus and minus figures alike. No other route has a deduction.
7. B combines the A entries of one pallet number into one line with that number as movement id and their summed quantity, sign reversed; their own movement id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
8. A combined line that is short by the exact quantity of one of its entries means that this one entry is missing from it and does not reconcile, while the rest of the pallet is fine.
9. B lists its lines in its own order, not in the order of A.
10. Lines of B whose movement id is neither a movement id of A nor a pallet number of A relate to other business and are ignored.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

state:
A field controller called dranven-38 is to receive modules from the module feed.

Conventions:
1. To order two versions, compare the first numbers, then the second, then the third, always as whole numbers, so 0.10.1 comes after 0.9.8 and 1.2.10 after 1.2.9. The same holds for the two-part runtime versions: 2.10 comes after 2.9.
2. After a module name come one or more bounds separated by commas, and every bound must hold: >=V at least V, >V newer than V, <=V at most V, <V older than V, ==V exactly V, !=V any version except V.
3. The proposed set installs cleanly when every pinned version is listed in the module feed, every requirement of every pinned version names a module that is pinned at a version meeting all of its bounds, the runtime of the target environment meets every runtime bound of every pinned version, and no conflict entry of a pinned version applies to another pin.
4. Only the entries of the pinned versions count; what the module feed says about other versions plays no part.
5. Nothing is installed besides the pins, so a requirement on a module without a pin is not met.
6. A pin that no pinned version requires does no harm by itself; its own entry is checked like that of every other pin.
7. A runtime bound of a pinned version is met when the runtime of the target environment satisfies it; 'any' sets no runtime bound.
8. Conflicts ('cannot be combined with'): a pinned version that names a module P with a bound blocks the set exactly when P is pinned at a version meeting that bound; if P has no pin, or its pin misses the bound, nothing happens.

q.instructions: Is the request allowed?

state:
Access export of an invented building access system. The rules in this export decide every request.

How access is decided:
1. An assignment gives one role to one user or to one group. An assignment to a group counts for every member of the group. Membership passes through nested groups: when group X is listed as a member of group Y, all members of X (also those X has through its own nested groups) are members of Y. It does not pass the other way: a user listed directly in Y is not thereby a member of X.
2. Assignments reach downward only: the zone where an assignment is made and everything below it, however deep, are covered; zones beside it or above it are not.
3. Exception for sealed zones: an assignment never passes into a sealed zone from a zone above it, so the sealed zone and everything below it stay out of its reach. A seal does nothing to an assignment made at the sealed zone or below it, and nothing to zones that are not inside the sealed zone.
4. Holding a role permits the actions on its own list and, when the role extends a second role, every action the second role permits (its own list and whatever it takes over by extension). The second role takes over nothing from the first.
5. Actions can include other actions, exactly as listed. Being allowed an action means being allowed every action it includes, directly or through a chain of listed inclusions. An inclusion is never read backwards, and actions without a listed link do not include each other.
6. A deny entry forbids one action to one user, or to all direct and nested members of one group, on one zone and all zones below it; seals make no difference to deny entries. When an entry matches the requester, the exact action and the zone, the request is refused whatever the assignments say. An entry for a different action never matches, and inclusions between actions are ignored for deny entries.
7. A request is allowed only when an assignment whose role the requester holds covers the requested zone and that role allows the requested action; in addition no deny entry may apply.

Actions: enter, escort, inspect, service, unlock, rekey

- The two class changes are cumulative: meeting rule 1 and rule 2 means two classes up, with class 1 as the limit.
- A booked time counts as due from its own minute on, that is, when it is not later than the current time.
- Two visitors that are both due, or both not due (no booked time, or one that is still to come), stay level under this rule.

Internal access policy

Rule 1. A request for which the requested access period is greater than 30 days and the contractor status flag is set to yes is denied.
Rule 2. A request for which the tenure does not exceed 365 days and the contractor status flag is set to yes is denied.
Rule 3. A request for which the tenure is lower than 30 days and the clearance level is under 2 is denied.
Rule 4. A request for which the contractor status flag is yes and the system class is not one of B, D or C is escalated to a human reviewer.
Rule 5. A request for which the requested access period is 90 days or higher is escalated to a human reviewer.
Rule 6. A request for which the record shows yes for the on-call duty flag and the clearance level is above 4 is approved.
Rule 7. A request for which the case has the contractor status flag set to no and the clearance level is more than 3 is approved.
Rule 8. A request for which the system class is either C, D or A and the tenure exceeds 365 days and the requested access period is lower than 30 days is approved.
Rule 9. A request for which the clearance level is lower than 3 and the system class is not A and the contractor status flag is set to yes is denied.
Rule 10. A request for which the clearance level is at most 3 and the system class is among B or D is escalated to a human reviewer.
Rule 11. A request for which the requested access period is 14 days or less and the record shows no for the contractor status flag is approved.
Rule 12. A request for which the tenure is at most 365 days and the clearance level is within 2 to 3 with both limits included is escalated to a human reviewer.

Exception to Rule 8: it is not applied when the clearance level is less than 2.
Exception to Rule 9: it is not applied when the requested access period is 14 days or less and the tenure exceeds 365 days.
Exception to Rule 7: it is not applied when the tenure is under 365 days.
Exception to Rule 10: it is not applied when the record shows no for the contractor status flag.

If two applicable rules lead to different outcomes, the higher-numbered rule decides.
If no rule applies, the request is approved.

Reconciliation for March 2026. Ledger A is the cash book kept by Prelansa Instruments; ledger B is the bank statement issued by Hosketh Savings Bank.

How the two ledgers are matched:
(1) Pairing goes by reference alone: an entry of A goes with the B line or lines showing the very same reference.
(2) Lines in B are not sorted the way A is; their position tells nothing.
(3) Lines of B whose reference is neither a reference of A nor a lodgement number of A relate to other business and are ignored.
(4) Signs are mirrored between the two ledgers: what is positive in A is negative in B, and what is negative in A is positive in B.
(5) An entry reconciles when the amount figure on its B line is its own amount figure with the sign reversed and the date rule holds. Split entries, entries with channel CARD and entries with a lodgement number follow their own rules below.
(6) A B line dated more than 5 days before or after its A entry is not a valid match, so that entry does not reconcile; 5 days or less is fine.
(7) An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its reference; it then reconciles when the two amount figures add up to its amount with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
(8) A line for an entry with channel CARD is 0.55 smaller in size in B (processing fee; size means the figure without its sign) than in A and carries the opposite sign: a plus of size S in A shows as a minus of size S less 0.55 in B, and a minus of size S in A as a plus of size S less 0.55. Other channel values carry no deduction.
(9) B combines the A entries of one lodgement number into one line with that number as reference and their summed amount, sign reversed; their own reference values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.
(10) When a combined line is smaller in size than the total by precisely the amount of one of its entries, only that entry fails to reconcile.

No more than one entry of A can fail; possibly none does.

state:
Booking sheet for the activity rooms of Marby Village Forum; 24-hour clock. Confirmed bookings stay as they are. The request is confirmed unchanged or not at all, which needs every rule to hold for it.

RULES
- Bookings on different days never clash.
- People are identified by their full name; a shared first or family name alone means nothing.
- A booking whose day field lists several days (like Mon/Thu) takes place on each of them, at the same time, in the same room, with the same people.
- The places of a room limit the group: host and guests together must fit. The host counts as one person and is not in the guests list; a full room is fine.
- No booking may start before its room opens or end after it closes. Starting at opening time or ending at closing time is fine.
- The end time of the request is its start time plus its duration.
- A room needs a reset between bookings whose length depends on its kind: if one booking ends at time T, the next booking of that room may start at T + gap or later, not before. No reset is needed after opening or before closing time.
- The request is confirmed only if its room has all the items it needs. Extra equipment does no harm; a similar item under another name does not help.
- A person, whether host or guest, cannot be in two bookings that overlap in time on the same day, even in different rooms. People need no gap: one activity may end at the very minute the person's next one starts.

The order is fixed by these rules, taken in the order given:
1. Waiting at least 40 minutes lifts a patient by one class.
2. A patient with a lower class number goes before a patient with a higher class number.
3. Shorter consultation time first.
4. If patients are still level, the lower ticket number is ahead.

How to read the rules:
- Read the rules from top to bottom; a later rule is used only to separate patients that every earlier rule leaves level.
- Rule 1 changes the class of a patient and is applied to every patient before anything is compared; in the rules after it, "class" means the class after this change.
- "Up one class" is the class number minus 1; for example, class 4 turns into class 3.
- There is no class above class 1, so a change that would lead above class 1 stops at class 1.
- A patient that has moved up is an ordinary member of its new class; nothing else about it changes.
- Waiting time = current time minus the time under "arrived", in minutes (same day, 24-hour clock).
- The limit itself counts: 40 minutes of waiting are enough, one minute less is not.
- All positions (first, second, third) refer to a single order computed at the current time; the clock is not moved in between.
- Columns and flags that no rule mentions have no effect on the order.
- Ticket numbers are the digits after the dash, compared as numbers, and they are unique.

q.instructions: Which entry of ledger A does not reconcile with ledger B?

state:
Reconciliation for July 2026. Ledger A is the dispatch register kept at the Yorvela plant; ledger B is the weighbridge record of the haulier Selvolm Haulage.

How the two ledgers are matched:
(1) An entry of A and a line of B belong together when their note id values are identical, character for character.
(2) All weight figures in B carry the sign opposite to the one in A.
(3) A pair agrees when the B weight figure equals the A weight figure multiplied by -1 and the dates are within the tolerance. The rules below cover the exceptions: split entries, packing PALLET entries and load entries.
(4) The date of a B line may be up to 2 days earlier or later than the date of its A entry; a gap of more than 2 days means the entry does not reconcile.
(5) An entry of A may appear in B as two lines with its note id; it then reconciles when the two weight figures add up to its weight with the sign reversed and both lines pass the date rule.
(6) For every A entry whose packing is PALLET, B takes a fixed pallet tare of 25.0 kg per line off the size of the figure (the figure without its sign), whether it is a plus or a minus: the size of the B figure is the size of the A figure less 25.0 kg, and the sign is the opposite one. Entries with any other packing are not reduced.
(7) B combines the A entries of one load number into one line with that number as note id and their summed weight, sign reversed; their own note id values do not appear in B, and the line must be within the date tolerance of their common date.

nuvmur-20 (an analysis workstation) should get the packages listed under the pins, drawn from the package index.

Rules of this check:
- To order two versions, compare the first numbers, then the second, then the third, always as whole numbers, so 0.10.1 comes after 0.9.8 and 1.2.10 after 1.2.9. Runtime versions (two parts) follow the same order, so 4.11 is later than 4.9.
- Each bound is an operator and a version: >= (that version or newer), > (newer only), <= (that version or older), < (older only), == (only that version), != (every version but that one); a list of bounds is met only when each bound is met.
- A clean install needs all of the following: each pin is a version that the package index lists; for each pinned version, each package it needs is pinned too, at a version inside the stated bounds; the runtime of the environment satisfies the runtime bounds of all pinned versions; no pinned version has a 'cannot be combined with' entry that applies to another pin.
- Requirements and other entries of versions without a pin do not matter.
- Nothing is installed besides the pins, so a requirement on a package without a pin is not met.
- Extra pins are fine: a pinned package that nothing requires is harmless as long as its own entry is satisfied.
- The environment's runtime must satisfy each runtime bound of each pinned version ('any' means no bound).
- An entry 'cannot be combined with P B' under a pinned version means that the set fails when P is pinned at a version meeting the bound B; it does not matter which of the two lists it, and an entry about a package without a pin, or whose pin misses B, does no harm.
